27046893.model_family: convolutional neural network (multi-scale patch and kernel sizes)
27046893.clinical_problem: automatic brain tissue segmentation for quantitative MRI analysis
27046893.patient_population: preterm infants scanned at 30 and 40 weeks postmenstrual age, alongside aging adults (~70y) and young adults (~23y) used as comparison cohorts
27046893.model_description: The model takes a single anatomical MR brain image as input and outputs a multi-class tissue segmentation. It is a convolutional neural network that combines multiple patch sizes and convolution kernel sizes to capture multi-scale voxel information, learning discriminative features from training data rather than relying on hand-crafted ones. It was evaluated across five separate cohorts spanning preterm infants and adults of different ages.
27046893.dataset_size: five datasets covering preterm infant MRI (30 and 40 weeks PMA, coronal and axial) and adult/young-adult MRI cohorts; exact per-group counts not stated
27046893.headline_result: Average Dice coefficients of 0.87, 0.82, 0.84, 0.86, and 0.91 across the five segmented datasets

28815363.model_description: Reveal NLP, a commercial natural language processing tool paired with an inference rules engine, scans radiologists' free-text ultrasound reports to flag studies as positive or negative for deep venous thrombosis.
